transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Since I saw that freeway accident, I feel like I’m moving through life in a fog, like I’m watching myself from the outside and nothing feels quite real. It happened about two weeks ago, and I just haven't been able to shake this feeling since then.
Since the accident, have you also had symptoms like feeling very panicked, having intrusive memories or nightmares, or avoiding reminders of the event, or is it mainly this foggy, unreal feeling?

It’s definitely not just the foggy feeling. Whenever I hear tires on wet pavement or see brake lights, I suddenly see that car flipping and the kid's bloody face, and my chest tightens up. I've also been taking side streets that add twenty minutes to my commute and leaving the room if anyone even mentions the accident.
Have you also been having nightmares or sudden flashbacks of the accident, or feeling constantly on edge and easily startled since it happened?

Yes, I have sudden daytime flashbacks where I see the car flipping and the teenager's bloody face as if I'm right back there. I'm also incredibly jumpy now—if someone walks up behind me at work or drops a box, I jump so hard my heart pounds and my hands shake for several minutes, leaving me feeling constantly on edge.
Have these symptoms lasted more than one month since the accident, or are they still within the first month?

It's only been about two weeks since the accident happened, so it is still within the first month. All of these feelings started right after that night on the freeway and they really haven't let up since.
Have your symptoms been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse since the accident?

They haven't let up at all and have stayed consistently bad since the accident. In fact, it feels like they are getting even harder to manage as the days go on, and I feel like I'm barely holding things together.
Have these symptoms lasted more than one month since the accident, or are they still within the first month?
As I mentioned, it has only been about two weeks since the crash, so it's still within the first month. The symptoms started immediately after it happened and have been constant ever since.
Have you started to feel emotionally numb or detached from other people, or like you’re avoiding thoughts and feelings about the accident because they’re too upsetting?

Yes, I feel very detached, like I'm watching myself from the outside, and my son even says I seem "on another planet" during dinner. I'm also doing everything I can to avoid thinking about it—I shut down conversations immediately if anyone brings up the crash, and I drive far out of my way to avoid the freeway because it's just too overwhelming.
Have you had these symptoms for more than one month since the accident, or are they still within the first month?
Yes, it is still within the first month. It has only been about two weeks since the accident happened, and these feelings have been constant ever since that night.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than one month since the accident, or are they still within the first month?
Like I've mentioned, it has only been about two weeks since the accident, so it is definitely still within the first month. It hasn't even been three weeks yet since that night on the freeway.
Have your symptoms been improving at all, or are they still severe and ongoing without any relief since the accident?
They haven't improved at all and have been ongoing without any relief. Everything started right after that freeway pileup about two weeks ago, and it has been constant ever since.

It is still within the first month, as the accident only happened about two weeks ago. These feelings started right after that night on the freeway and haven't let up since.

It is still within the first month. The accident only happened about two weeks ago, and all of these symptoms started immediately after that night.

It is still within the first month. The accident was only about two weeks ago, and all of these feelings have been ongoing since that night.
Have you been having any periods where you lose awareness of what’s happening around you or feel like you can’t remember parts of the accident or what you did afterward?

I do frequently feel spaced out and detached, like I'm watching myself from the outside, and I'll find myself staring at my work screen without processing what I'm doing. However, I don't have any memory loss about the accident itself; those memories are unfortunately very vivid and clear.

It is still within the first month, as the accident happened just about two weeks ago. Honestly, because these feelings have been so constant and overwhelming, it feels like it has been going on for much longer than that.

Yes, I feel that way most of the time. It is like I'm watching myself from outside my body and everything around me is muted and far away, almost like I'm in a movie. This happens even during my normal routines, like when I'm talking to customers at the store, making dinner, or sitting at my pottery wheel.
